profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record at 2223 East Magnolia Street in the Central City area of Phoenix, Arizona, is tagged as a data center under the plainly descriptive name Data Storage Centers, a generic label rather than a distinctive brand name that is easy to independently verify. The address sits in an industrial corridor southeast of downtown Phoenix near Sky Harbor International Airport, an area with light industrial and warehouse buildings rather than the large hyperscale campuses that cluster elsewhere in the Phoenix metropolitan area, one of the largest and fastest growing data center markets in the United States. Searches for a company operating under the name Data Storage Centers at this address did not turn up a verifiable operator website, business registration record or press coverage confirming the building's current use, ownership or any technical specifications. It remains possible that a small colocation, backup or records storage business genuinely operates from this address under a generic descriptive name, consistent with the building's location in an industrial part of a major data center market, but that could not be confirmed. This entry records the building's tagged name and location honestly while leaving its operator, scale and current use as unverified rather than asserting figures that have no confirmed source.

reading.body:
This Phoenix facility has no published power specifications and no verified operator, so it cannot be counted as AI infrastructure; its 0 MW is one of 52 Arizona data centers that disclose nothing about power.

Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, but only 4 publish power specifications, totaling 512 MW of disclosed capacity. This facility's 0 MW is not a measured output; it is the absence of a published figure. Its industrial location near Sky Harbor places it in a major market, but location alone does not establish compute capacity or grid load.

For AI, the binding constraint is power, and a data center that publishes no megawatts cannot be added to any estimate of available compute or demand. The 512 MW disclosed across four Arizona facilities is the only public basis for assessing the state's data center power footprint; the other 52 mapped facilities, including this one, are invisible to that calculation.

The absence of an operator, website, or specifications does not prove the building is idle or not a data center. It may be a small colocation, backup, or records storage business under a generic name. Without direct confirmation from an operator or permitting records, its actual role, scale, and power draw remain unknown.
